name: encoding-reflection-through-program-values
description: A value reaches a destination through the program's own values: a type argument of a generic function of a destination package, a value of a type parameter's type, which is a value of each type argument the program instantiates it with, an interface-typed parameter of a function of the program that hands it to a destination, whatever its type, and an interface-typed result of a function of the program, which holds each concrete value its return statements store there; a call through a function value returns what every function or method of the program used as a value returns there, a bound method value among them. An encoder reads an embedded struct field whether or not its type is exported. A value returned as an interface and never encoded, and a value a function literal returns, reach nothing.
